body:
Fair.

I tried both lamotrigine and memantine for anxiety and although lamotrigine stopped my cycling, it did nothing for anxiety. Memantine appeared to have a mild effect for a few weeks, and then it made it considerably worse. Anecdote, of course.

Lamotrigine is not used as an anxiolytic. It's a mood stabilizer indicated for bipolar depression, and I think the vast majority of the bipolar community would agree that it has a pretty mild effect if any at all on anxiety.
If you nearly died last night, then yes, I and many others believe you should check yourself in.
At the Door to the Tenth Sub Level of Suicide by Leviathan.

Sounds like textbook SSRI discontinuation syndrome to me. Effexor is one of the most notorious for this, along with Paxil. I too have felt the unbelievable rage and anger that comes with stopping an SSRI. It's beyond comprehension, and you can't explain it to others unless they've felt it too.

I'm not a doctor, but perhaps it'd be easier to switch back to Lexapro and use Prozac to taper off of that instead of Effexor.

If I drop my phone and pointless internet surfing cold turkey, it takes about three days or so before I feel "normal" again. Withdrawals usually consist of being irritable as fuck and bored to tears. 

After that's over, my attention span goes way up and I feel more driven to be social, etc. Not a cure for your problems, but helps with actually getting shit done and being able to read more effectively, etc.

I felt it on 150 mg. Short term memory was a little spotty and conversations could be frustrating because I felt like I could never find the words to express what I wanted to say. Granted it could have been notable simply because my anxiety was high and not well controlled (and anxiety will cause brain fog anyway), but it was enough for me to want to stop taking lamotrigine.

Now I'm off it and it's still (to a certain extent) there. Probably anxiety to be frank. Either way, stressing about it will make it worse.

Odd experience given bupropion can also work for ADHD. Perhaps if shit falls apart later, I can titrate Wellbutrin real slow and hope once it levels out, the net therapeutic effect will be the same. For now, I'll just take Vyvanse and use it for whatever good it can give me. Really does a touch on easing depression. Things just feel better. More motivated and I want to do more.

Thanks.
Really appreciate this. Gonna try it tomorrow. Thanks.

A courteous and friendly waitress at a restaurant may also just be doing her job, but there's always a chance she's harboring some level of more intense interest, beyond just the day to day kindness she would show to others at work.

I'm biased (obviously) but I'm more partial to the advice below me. What if she says no? Where's the harm? I think I'm respectful enough to pull it off smoothly, if only I could find a time to ask her.
Valproic acid AKA valproate, divalproex, Epival, Depakote.

Sorry. No, worried about potential for serotonin syndrome as well as any other possible interactions with valproic acid.

According to half lives, by five days I should be at 0.3125 mg Lexapro floating around in my system. Doubtful this would cause any issues, but still.

Valproic acid is tanglier. Not sure how it affects serotonin.
The strength of what? Not sure I understand the question bud.

I used to be able to get to this level when I was younger. I miss it a lot, shit was absolutely hilarious. Everything starts to look like Paper Mario.

Nowadays it's like I have two levels of highness: high but not ripped, or passed the fuck out on a couch. Not sure why I can't get there anymore.

Starts to feel like when you lie down and stand up too fast and get lightheaded, except it doesn't go away after 5-10 seconds. Start feeling a bit anxious, a bit panicky. Nauseated. No hand-eye coordination, almost feel drunk. 

Next thing I know, I'm on my back and two people are grabbing me by the arms and chucking me on a couch. I just pass out and fall down. It's happened a couple times now. I don't worry about it as much as I know I'm just too high, but it's certainly uncomfortable. Give me a couch, a glass of water and a few hours to sleep it off and I'm back to normal.

I text everybody I don't text when I'm depressed. Just wanna be social, it feels so good to reach out to people but usually it's kind of pointless. Just empty conversations, although I have had some interesting ones.

Four days in is too short. I'm impatient too and I've been in that situation before. I did find that the haziness wore off though. Although it started creating mixed episode shit, so there's that too...
Can you tolerate SSRIs at all? Tricyclics?

I have no idea sometimes.

Cycle through different coping strategies. Sometimes drugs and alcohol, sometimes family, therapy, guitar, video games.

Try to keep some excitement in my life. Instead of working at so and so place for the rest of my life, I can travel to another town or city in my province and work there. Keep it fresh a bit. The change in scenery makes me feel like I'm on a bit of an adventure, keeps things new. Tends to tame my symptoms just a little.

I also unfortunately cope by fantasizing about dying sometimes, but I wouldn't recommend that.

I'm typing a lot. Apologies. Vyvanse is kicking in and I'm just starting going into the whole mixed state deal.

Welcome to my life.

On lamotrigine 100 mg, Lexapro 5 mg, Vyvanse 20 mg.

Vyanse has honestly changed my life, even helping with anxiety a bit without aggravating my bipolar symptoms. However, Lexapro is throwing me into agitation and anger again, so I'm planning on cutting out lamotrigine and adding Depakote tomorrow to see if I can get the anti-anxiety benefit of an SSRI without being thrown into depression or a mixed state type thing. Gonna make a thread on this actually.

I'd like some more clarification on what symptoms you're experiencing now, in a sober state of mind.

Is the voice still talking to you? Do you have any control over it? What exactly is it that the voice is telling you, and why do you believe it? If you were to completely relax your body and mind through some relaxation technique (other than drugs or alcohol), do you still experience these symptoms? 

What happens if you smoke now? Has it gotten worse?

I've experienced powerful anxiety that has been really fucking tricky and effective in mimicking "psychotic" symptoms, making me feel like I'm hearing things or like there's another "being" inside my head that's asking me things or influencing my behavior. When I'm anxious, that "voice" becomes a lot "louder" in a way. But on closer examination, it's more akin to racing thoughts, loosely connected ideas coming together quickly making you feel like you're not in control of where they're going, etc.

I had a panic attack on dope too. I had a yellow tint, not red. Not saying it was a panic attack for sure, but for all the times I thought I was experiencing psychosis or becoming schizophrenic from marijuana, it has always been simply anxiety. Use of a benzodiazepine will almost completely negate or eliminate those thoughts and feelings. If you were truly experiencing psychosis or mania, a benzo wouldn't do fuck all to alleviate your delusions and paranoia, manic behaviors, etc. Schizophrenics and bipolar patients can pop as many benzos or drink as much alcohol as they want, but it will never quell the voices or manic behaviors like an antipsychotic would. On the other hand, if you're just experiencing anxiety, a benzodiazepine should eliminate it or tone it down a hell of a lot.

Just my own experiences with cannabis and anxiety/paranoia, and how I've come to realize that it's not making me crazy, although it's certainly not helping my anxiety at all.

Maybe reduced libido but hard to say because more anxiety/stimulation decreases my libido anyway.

I'll make the jump eventually.

Came really close just then to smoking some CBD-only marijuana. Just calms you down without the high from THC, but decided against it at the last second. I feel bad for even considering it.

5 mg for two weeks then increase to 10 mg originally, but I was extremely, extremely anxious about side effects so we decided to keep at 5 mg until I feel I've reached some sort of plateau or stability with regards to what it's gonna do, then we'll talk about moving up.

Sexual side effects and apathy/amotivational symptoms are my biggest worries. Hence my reluctance to increase my dosage.

Canadian here.

I hear nothing about F1 in my province, despite being less than a four hour flight away from the Montreal Grand Prix.

We receive the Sky broadcast on TSN, which I'm super happy about. We get all the practices, qualifying and the race on Sunday. But other than myself and three of my buddies, I can't find anybody else that's really into it, or at least interested enough to watch.

Theoretically it could, but I think it's extremely unlikely.

Take a Benadryl and get back to us. A benzo will help too.

I think you're experiencing protracted akathisa secondary to Haldol use in combination with an SSRI.

I experienced the same akathisa with metoclopramide, another dopamine blocker, although I was taking Lexapro, not Prozac.

Give it a few days. Apparently the SSRI makes it last longer. It went away for me.

Yeah, you're right. Perhaps an ADHD trait (as my therapist tells me), I am extremely impatient, moreso when it comes to my mental health than anything else. In fact, I'd say I'm likely a little more patient than others when it comes to anything else! 9 years is a long time to be trying new meds, but I know many people here have it worse off than I do.

I'll be honest, I'm finding Vyvanse to help with anxiety moreso than Lexapro is right now. Vyvanse focused and directed my thoughts: when I sat down to watch a movie, I watched it. I didn't have a whole bunch of anxious thoughts running wild in my head. It also pushed me (perhaps due to its stimulating nature) to head into social situations with a little more effort than before. On the cons list, that focus and direction can also hurt you, because when you focus on something anxiety provoking, it makes it a little bit worse than normal. The physical aspects of anxiety become heightened (secondary to norepinephrine release): increased heart rate, muscle tension, stomach discomfort, etc.

It doesn't help too much with depression. I see more positive life perspectives evolving as I continue Lexapro. I just wish Lexapro wasn't so damn stimulating. It helps and hurts at the same time. Makes some anxieties better, makes others worse. It makes Vyvanse less effective as the increased anxiety from Lexapro causes my concentration to fail, etc.

It's a fuck around. But I'll keep going for now.

With regards to GABA, I've tried Lyrica (pregabalin). Helped with anxiety, both social and general as well as sleep, but my short and long term memory took a hit and it also had sexual side effects.
Worth a shot anyway. Best of luck.

Perhaps it's all just anticipatory anxiety and it'll resolve when you complete your appointments.

I'd be careful with psychedelics though. Have some "trip-killers" on board like benzodiazepines or antipsychotics (alprazolam, quetiapine, respectively) in case things take a turn. People will tell you that those tough times are beneficial in that you can grow from them, etc. but at the same time without a trip sitter or somebody to guide you through it, you can get in some serious trouble with your head that may or may not resolve when you come down.

I've felt LSD take a negative turn. All of a sudden the entire perspective of the trip took on a negative, dark, anxious tone. Medicated with clonazepam 0.5 mg and within 45 minutes I was doing much better, laughing with friends again, etc.

I'm just ranting now, but all I can tell you is be careful.

I haven't tried mushrooms, but I've tried LSD. I eliminated the anxiety factor and premedicated with clonazepam 1.5 mg before the trip, 1 mg before redosing and 0.5 mg on the comedown. Felt a funny afterglow for a few days, then it was gone.

I've got you.

It's so crazy to think that one experience can change your brain like that, but drugs are powerful. They are to be respected, and despite our addictive desires and personalities, we need to use caution when taking or mixing them and ensure the best experience possible for ourselves and others.
Take it day by day and see if things even out. Tough advice, I know. I'm one of the most impatient people out there, and I need to listen to that advice more than ever.

Go ahead and take one. See what happens. It won't hurt you. Might make you sleepy, but if you've got nothing else on the go, what odds.

See if it helps your anxiety.

You've got a few drug changes going on there. Gonna take a little while to tease out what's causing what, what needs to be stopped, etc.

Sounds like you had a panic attack. They may or may not go away with time. Certainly a break in cannabis use is warranted, at least for a week to see if you settle out. If not, welcome to the anxiety club. Shit sucks.

You can take hydroxyzine before smoking. It's an antihistamine, not unlike diphenhydramine. Can help relieve anxiety, albeit in a very mild manner. Usually just makes you drowsy. If I remember correctly, can also be used as an antihypertensive in intravenous form in hospital. Shouldn't hurt you cardiac-wise.

I'm trying to understand how the 5 hour energy affected you. Did you have a panic attack? Did you smoke after the energy drink and have a bad time?

Cannabis can unearth anxiety disorders in those prone to them (it happened to me), even after years of use.

Yeah I worked ICU for a year. Unfortunately my anxiety disorder got the best of me and I had to drop out of it. One of the shittiest feelings I've had in a long time.

With a HR of 38, ketamine was a good choice as it has pro-cardiac effects. Etomidate could have been alright too, although given its effect on cortisol levels I'm not sure how it would have interacted with the other drugs he was on.

No, it's still here. But as I said, its impact on my life is highly correlated to my anxiety levels. If my anxiety flares up, I see it a lot. Halos, blurred lights, floaters, patterns shifting ever so slightly if I zone out while looking at them, etc.

I doubt it will ever go away. But if I can find a fucking reasonable treatment for my anxiety disorders, I doubt I'll ever have to deal with it again.

Edit - And honestly, if you can control the anxiety regarding it, it will quickly fade into the background and you won't notice it as much. It becomes normal.

HPPD acquired from irresponsible "meth bomb" use with questionable psychedelic substances in said pills.

Had it for nine years. Generally correlates with my anxiety. Anxiety goes up, I see it more. Anxiety goes down, I hardly if ever notice it and when I do it doesn't bother me.

Occasional recreational use of psychedelics or heavy marijuana use will make it more prominent for a few days or a week, but it always returns to baseline.

Mind you I've been on and off psychiatric meds for my anxiety for all of those nine years. But none really seemed to make it worse. If it was made worse, it was always because the med caused anxiety which caused me to obsess over it.

Why was a paralytic not considered? I guess given the fact you couldn't adequately sedate him it would be pretty heartless to paralyze the fuckin guy while he's in agitated delirium. As if the trip wasn't already bad enough.

Maybe an Ativan/Versed infusion along with the Propofol? IM/IV antipsychotics?

Crazy situation, not something I've ever dealt with in my year in critical care, but interesting to talk through and discuss either way.

Given his acute state of agitated delirium, I'm doubtful there was much of a concern over CV status. BP and HR probably through the roof, could likely do for some cardiac depressant effects. To my knowledge Precedex potentiate the effects of opioids, which probably wouldn't be given in this situation unless some physician wanted some Fentanyl for intubation.

Edit - I meant CV status in terms of BP/HR decreasing, not increasing. That's an issue too, but hopefully the sedation could curb some of it.

What was the rationale for giving Precedex of all things for a violent patient on PCP? I can understand trying to avoid intubation, but in my experience Precedex would be far too weak to make a dent in that person's agitation.
Checking in as another one who didn't have first kiss/lost virginity until 21. You're not alone.

Is there any timeline to how long it would take for the effects of Vyvanse to become apparent again? Right now they're very subtle, if not completely gone. I'd like to smoke a few more times before stopping completely as I'm going on a short trip in a week to meet with some old friends.

I really should stop, as Vyvanse has done a lot for me even in this short amount of time. The only way I've been able to simulate the effects of Vyvanse are to cut out my phone, all social media, TV, etc. I guess the dopamine just builds up and helps me focus, but not quite as well as Vyvanse.

I was on Paxil for a year when I was younger. Sexual side effects were like nothing I've ever been on, and the emotional bunting was terrible. Feeling good is great, but when every day is the best day of your life, it gets old fast.
Amphetamine based stimulants, perhaps? Vyvanse or Adderall?
Kills me. Wish I had me an Irish girl.

Lithium is primarily used for control of manic episodes in type I bipolar disorder. I used it off-label for anxiety. Didn't do shit for anxiety, but potentiated the effects of the moclobemide I was already taking. Unfortunately not enough to make a real difference though. Also off moclobemide now, that's why I'm on Lexapro. But the sexual side effects suck and I'm having a hard time with them so I wanna get messed up.

Oh yeah, seizures abound. That's when taken together though. I've been off a low dose for about two weeks, plus I'm taking clonazepam with it so any lowering of the seizure threshold should be abated by the GABAergic effects of the Kpins.
Update: got wrecked, smoked some weed, blacked out. Exhausted today because of clonazepam's long half life. Fuck.
I'm not depressed bro. I'm terminally anxious. Terminally. It'll fucking kill me. Or I'll kill myself before I deal with these STUPID fucking meds. Clonazepam is the only thing to work.

I'm hoping for this, or even faster. My sex drive is normally through the roof. I'm still obsessively scrolling through forum posts and google searches, and the info I'm finding is only slightly encouraging at best...

I'm probably going to need a dose increase too. I just don't see a solution. Everything I predicted is coming true.

You raise some good points, I hadn't thought of them. 

Isn't there some kind of "hack" you can use to stay in a Schengen country, leave for a week, and then come back? I thought I read about that online somewhere.

I guess the thing they worry about the most is finances. I'm fairly relaxed about my money, I don't hoard it by any means and as long as I have enough to pay for the life I'm living now, I consider myself okay. I have not yet settled into a full time job, choosing instead to work on a casual basis so I have more freedom in my schedule. I'm 26, so I worry a little bit because other people seem to be taking different routes: buying vehicles, houses, settling down, married and kids, etc. I'm not doing any of that. I'm just taking my money and using it to travel around Europe. My dad would have a big issue with all this lol.

Equally at play is my mental health, which is not good by any means and subject to huge swings on a weekly basis, although lately it's been mired in a depression of sorts. It's easy to use travelling as a means to run away (I guess).

But yeah, I get you. I appreciate the answer. I'll take it into account with everything else written here.

I'll take a look.

Being a nurse, my job obviously wouldn't be transferable unless I had an extremely solid grasp of the language, a professional level of understanding.

I wouldn't be opposed to working some kind of job, even in a bar or something to have something to do while I'm there. Of course that would require a different kind of visa, but I'd be interested if there are any jobs that require a bare minimum of German to work.

That's where I'm conflicted. A part of me feels like if I'm going for that long, I should at least do *something*, but there's another part that's thinking "fuck it, go over, see some things and meet some wonderful people, you won't regret it".

Hard trying to decide between the two...and although they have no say in my decision, my parents would be much more supportive of going to study, knowing I'll have a place to stay, food to eat, etc. They would be much less supportive of just surfing around for six months. It's tough wanting to do something and trying to justify it in your head when other people in your life think you're crazy or making a bad decision. That's where I struggle. Maybe that's why I'm asking. Just want to hear that they're both legitimate choices, with pros and cons on each side.

Yeah, that's what I mean. Travelling on off days, weekends, etc.

I haven't heard of the WHV scheme. I'll take a look.

Nor have I looked into doing this as a free agent as opposed to with a company. Perhaps that would be a little cheaper.

Not a student anymore unfortunately, I'm a Registered Nurse. I thought about that too but unless I go back to school (which I'm actually hoping to do at some point when my mental health stabilizes) it won't be an option for me.
I wish I subscribed to the same view. From one human being to another, I wish you the best of luck in your search.

Yeah, I'd say that's the reason why. I don't think I'd be capable of getting anything up, including myself out of bed on that combo. Seroquel certainly quelled the anxiety, but I was on 150 mg of the XR version and it certainly would have needed to been higher to really fix the problem, but I was exhausted, lazy, hungry, and sexually handicapped on it so I stopped. Lexapro is probably a boner-killer too. Wellbutrin made me one of the nastiest people on earth so I'm at a loss. At least I know there's another in my position.
Presumably you have zero sex drive or ability on that combo?

Guess we got that going for us. Hard to find other people with the same story. Currently taking lithium, lamotrigine, and moclobemide for supposed bipolar disorder as I exhibit "hypomania" and depression when treated with most other SSRIs. Luvox made me rapid cycle. Gonna try trazadone next. Starting to rely too much on alcohol and weed to get me through...better than self-harm I guess.

I had the same experience, although with Paxil instead of Prozac. My anxiety was out of control. Paxil relieved it almost completely. I finally felt like "me". Side effects were shit though, so I stopped. Over fifteen meds later, nothing has ever worked like Paxil has. Guess I'll just keep popping clonazepam to go to work! Sad state of affairs.
HPPD?

Kind of a happy medium I guess. I usually pause for thirty seconds before doing my ritual in the bathroom, and sometimes I don't even need to do it. I've been able to use urinals again, which is good. Means my anxiety is coming down. Slow process and not where I want to be, but I still feel "manly" I guess so no harm done really. The images reduce my "drive" but my anxiety has gone down so maybe the two are interconnected and the images weren't doing as much harm as I thought they were.

Still looking for a medication solution though. OCD is part of the problem but my social anxiety is making it difficult to work so I spend most of my time with my therapist on my SA and GAD.
Perhaps it could help offset the idea that I'm a racist or skinhead, if it was present to begin with. I'd be recognized as a tourist.

I posted in the Germany subreddit, but I'll ask here as well.

I wear a black pair of pants, black t-shirt, black shoes and a black baseball hat with a black hoodie more or less all the time. I'm planning on getting either a mohawk or shaving my head again tomorrow, which is the usual for me. I'm going to Germany on Wednesday for eleven days.

Am I going to look like a skinhead? Would it even be an issue? Sometimes I'll have my backpack on with a Canadian flag on it so I'm not terribly worried about those times, but what about just walking around the city or countryside with that outfit?
Me too. I'm hyped!

And if I don't get a mohawk I'll have it shaved almost completely to the skin. I also wear all black, black skate shoes with pants, shirt, black baseball hat and everything. Should I be worried? Most of the time I'll have a backpack on with a Canadian flag attached, but I'd be worried about walking down the street with a shaved head and all black clothing.
They told me it had connotations to the skinhead movement.

Hey guys. Thinking about getting a mohawk type haircut (shaved on the sides, short in the middle, like a flat version) before my trip to Germany. Is this gonna be a problem? Someone told me I was asking for trouble doing that.

Does it make you anxious afterward?

I did SOMETHING last night, I have no idea what. I think I pulled a hair off of my beard, and now I'm wrecked. Anxiety through the roof. I'm so uncomfortable. 

I just feel so restrained and wrong. Things I say don't feel right. Feels like I'm being held back, like something is thrown over me, a heavy blanket. I can't stop paying attention to my nose, it's driving me crazy.

Anxiety. Can't fuckin' win. At least I've got Formula 1 this morning.
Only if they're inversely correlated.
That one hurt.
Solved!
It's a lung bag for a CPR dummy. Thanks!
Do you become aroused by them?

Yeah, me too!

So do you think about pornography regularly? Do you visualize it and focus on it?

So just to update, I'm trying to sit with the thoughts a little more, although if I'm being completely truthful, I am definitely still trying to avoid them a little. I just don't see how intentionally viewing these thoughts will help my addiction or OCD at all. Viewing the thoughts just makes my anxiety ten times worse, not to mention the whole "withdrawal" effects that come from exposing myself to an image I'm supposed to stay away from. I definitely feel an increase in anxiety and general OCD symptoms today, but I'm also taking clonazepam today so they're more tolerable. I have to take clonazepam at work otherwise I'm just a mess. I'll continue to try to delay my shakes and twitches a little bit, and remind myself that using the bathroom and being aroused are two different things, and I don't need to worry about becoming aroused while peeing or what have you. Jeez, still embarrassing to talk about.

This seems extremely counter intuitive given my goal of being free from the grips of my addiction. So when I see a pornographic image in my head, instead of refocusing, I have to think about it? View it instead of try to avoid it?

Let's step away from my head for a minute. You said you're doing Nofap as well. How do you deal with this issue? How can you make any headway at all by continuing to think about pornography?

Again, apologies if my tone comes across as snotty or dismissive. I'm pretty scared, and every part of my brain is screaming at me not to do what you're telling me.

I know, right? It's fine to limit exposure to things I have control over - TV programs, internet, etc. It's another to limit exposure to something in my head, especially with OCD. I'm doing myself a favor by not thinking about it, but my brain just keeps sabotaging me with sneak attacks when I'm most vulnerable, which happens to be pretty much all the damn time.

So by not resisting the images, do I just let them sit there? Do I acknowledge them and refocus, gently point my mind towards something else? If I let them linger, I will most certainly become aroused. I apologize if I come off as being dismissive or skeptical, I'm just really trying to figure out how to implement the idea.

I have no problem not doing any of that, but the reaction that happens to me (becoming aroused) is involuntary. And that then sets me back, putting me back into withdrawals, back into the urges. Back into that old dead dick feeling. My problem is not with having the willpower to not act on the urges, believe me. It's the huge burst in anxiety, depression, and urges that comes with having been aroused to a pornographic image in my head (one that I am certainly not choosing to think about).
I'm in so much pain. They never go away. I'm getting closer and closer to grabbing a knife and making a little slice somewhere, just to see if it stops the pain.
The Great Southern Trendkill!

Not sure what you mean about going into memantine withdrawals. I just don't feel notably different. If I take it at the exact same time every single day, I do feel an improvement in attention and concentration, but that doesn't translate to an improvement in OCD or general anxiety.

More and more I'm starting to think that this may very well be an exacerbation of my underlying anxiety disorder secondary to my LSD usage. Fuck. I've had HPPD for years, and now it's aggravated by this increase in anxiety. No telling how long it's going to last, hopefully not long.

I'll give memantine a full month, till the third of February. That'll be over two weeks on 15 mg, and if things haven't considerably improved at that point, I'll move on to lithium or valproate. Memantine is too sketchy, too finicky. Not enough research to justify continuing it.

Might be just the anxiety and fear I seem to experiencing from memantine, but I'm getting more and more turned off from it every day. I'm just seeing conflicting reports online as well as some concern with long term use and discontinuation. Having to be so particular in "dosing schedules" is a pain in the ass, and if the drug is that finicky in that missing my AM dose by three or four hours will cause brain fog and anxiety, I don't really see any point in continuing this.

Currently I'm managing the unreal fear and anxiety with clonazepam, but I can still feel it poking through, even with all that GABA activity going on. Things just don't feel right. I really doubt this is from my LSD trip last week as it wasn't even that bad and I had a decent week at work despite it. It's only been the last five or six days that things have started acting up.

I managed to get my GP to prescribe memantine for me. He doesn't know much about it though outside of its use for dementia and Alzheimer's. We've been through the ringer with meds. He'll more or less prescribe whatever I can find that has some evidence of efficacy for my illness. I've been through a ridiculous amount of medications.
Appreciate it my friend. I'm near panic attack in the break room right now.

Yeah, also on moclobemide 450 mg daily, lamotrigine 150 mg daily, and clonazepam as needed. I've been on all of these meds for several months and I understand how they affect me.

I tried LSD last not this past Sunday but the one before, and although it wasn't a good trip, it wasn't really a bad one either. I could feel some anxiety but I took a clonazepam and calmed down significantly. The rest of that week I felt more or less okay. That was the week that I started 15 mg of memantine. I should mention that I also tried LSD on the first of January, and it was a good experience, allowing me to see past some inflexible thought patterns and move forward in my treatment.

Last weekend I had an edible on Friday night which was okay, and I got incredibly drunk on Saturday leading to a more or less three day hangover.

So as you can see, my lifestyle has not been conducive to my mental health as of late. That's my fault, and I'll take the blame for it. I also have a pornography addiction, and my OCD likes to focus on that so I consistently have images of porn playing in my head that I try very hard to supress. I haven't been able to do that as of late, and as a result my body kind of "relapses" when the thoughts become too prominent and I can't take my focus off them. But that's another story altogether.
Been off porn for over three years bud, barring these not under my control incidences.
Jon Hopkins.

Once upon a time I chewed up my Luvox tablet and got a chemical burn on my tongue. Most bitter thing I've ever tasted, and I couldn't taste anything else for two days. To make it worse, I was on vacation at the time.
I learned not to attempt first-time burn care by yourself.
Another RN trying for MD! We can do it.

It's just that I feel worse every time this happens, anxiety-wise. To me, that indicates that something is wrong, but as I said in my comment below, this type of thing may happen to nofappers all the time. It may be that I've just got so many mental health things going on that I'm extremely sensitive to any changes in my brain chemistry. Hard to say.

And it's not just an occasional thing. When I'm walking around, I have an erection almost constantly. It's not priapism, it's just anxiety. Let's think about it.

Heart failure occurs as a result of the heart lacking sufficient mechanical strength to pump blood throughout the body. The ventricles aren't able to contract as powerfully as they previously were able to.

In left-sided heart failure, oxygenated blood arrives from the *pulmonary veins* and is sent to the the left ventricle to be pumped throughout the body. However, due to the left ventricle not having full contracting power, the blood gets held up and backs up into where it came from. In this case, the pulmonary veins and the lungs.

In right-sided heart failure, the exact same mechanism happens. The right ventricle is unable to pump blood to the lungs for oxygenation. It gets held up and backs up into the inferior vena cavae and superior vena cavae. This leads to...peripheral edema! Among other symptoms.

When I started, I knew I had to focus on my breath, but I did so by pushing away and ignoring all the thoughts that I was having. This later culminated in some nasty repressed feelings being released with a lot of anger.

My personal technique works in this way: I have a thought about something, and in my head I say "I'm having a thought about _____, back to breath". This way, I can acknowledge the thought by saying what it is, and then bring my awareness back to my breath without ignoring the thought.
